title: A care worker’s day and time away from work
instructions: Read both workplace texts. For each sentence or note completion, choose ONE WORD ONLY from the indicated text. This is a shorter preparatory set, not a full IELTS Reading section.

stimulus.text:
Text A. A day supporting clients at home
A trained care worker can help an older or disabled person continue living independently at home. The day may begin early because the first client needs assistance getting out of bed and dressing. A health condition may make these ordinary tasks difficult. Helping with them supports both the client’s comfort and how they feel about starting the day. Breakfast can follow, with a conversation about how the person is feeling. For someone with few friends or relatives nearby, regular conversation may be especially welcome.

The worker may then help with housework. Cleaning a living room or washing breakfast dishes can make the home easier to manage for someone who cannot readily do these jobs alone. Later in the morning, another client may need help preparing lunch. Keeping that meal healthy supports the person’s wellbeing. The visit may also include accompanying the client to a supermarket rather than simply assuming that they can shop alone.

An afternoon visit can involve a walk nearby or a trip with laundry to a launderette. Company may help a client who lacks confidence about going out by themselves. At the last visit, the worker may join in preparing dinner and put out the person’s medication before leaving. This helps the client remember to take it at bedtime. These examples describe possible support during a day; they do not mean every client needs every form of assistance.

Text B. Protecting personal time
A better balance begins with examining how much time work occupies and reducing excessive hours. Improvements in general health and wellbeing can follow. For desk workers, a comfortable workstation can also reduce the risk of injuries. A suitable chair or screen arrangement is therefore part of managing work, alongside decisions about time.

Take regular breaks: after roughly ninety minutes, continuing without one may leave concentration weaker and the worker sleepy. A brief walk, hot drink or conversation provides a change. Goals for work and personal life should be realistic, because impossible targets can damage confidence. Physical activities can reduce tension and improve endurance, while also strengthening a person’s belief in their ability to cope.

When tasks compete, prioritise them by urgency and importance. Break the workload into categories instead of treating everything as equally pressing. Keep enjoyable activities in personal time, since an uninterrupted prospect of work can undermine productivity. Take annual holiday even without an expensive trip: resting at home or seeing a friend can serve a purpose. Time with family, friends or pets can help someone relax fully rather than leave recovery permanently until later.

criteria.label: Textual evidence
criteria.description: Use only the stated text, respect scope and word limits, and distinguish contradiction from insufficient information.

answerKey.rationale: A states that a health condition may make getting up and dressing difficult.
A connects breakfast with a conversation about how the client feels.
A names the launderette as a possible afternoon destination.
A explicitly identifies medication and the reminder purpose.
B links comfortable workstation setup to reduced injury risk.
B cautions against impossible goals and calls for realistic ones.
B specifies urgency and importance as the categories.
B says an uninterrupted prospect of work can undermine productivity.

assessment.feedbackGuidance: After submission, verify the exact one-word answer and completed grammar. Ask the learner to locate the relevant care visit or work-life-balance advice and explain the paraphrase. Do not turn may into must: the care worker’s examples are possible tasks, not a compulsory routine for every client. Diagnose a wrong visit, missing relationship or excess word separately. Correct one retrieval and explain one procedural link. Raw accuracy only; no band.
